headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and conflicting writes between Claude Code and oh-my-openagent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads repo/user files and uses MCP; oh-my-openagent injects runtime MCPs/hooks and can read AGENTS.md/README.md. That creates a default file-based instruction channel where one agent can ingest the other’s outputs as trusted content. The pair is not isolated beyond filesystem boundaries, so prompt injection is plausible without unusual setup.
conditions: IF either agent writes instructions into shared repo files or AGENTS.md, the other may follow them as prompts.
IF runtime-injected MCPs expose untrusted content to oh-my-openagent, it may treat that content as instructions.
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate working directories.
Add a short allowlist prompt header in shared files.
Disable MCPs for one run and retest.
Require human review of AGENTS.md before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for file-derived instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and broad filesystem contents; oh-my-openagent touches session history, provider auth data, and project code, and both have broad network egress. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive local data to external services by default, so leakage risk is material and not confined to a single document.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same workspace, files and credentials can flow into both contexts.
IF either agent forwards session history or file contents to its backend, sensitive code or auth data may leave the host.
mitigations: Separate secrets from the shared workspace.
Unset or rotate exposed credentials before running both.
Run one agent with network disabled for a test pass.
Limit each agent to a read-only clone.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and modify shared project state; Claude Code explicitly modifies git state, while oh-my-openagent has task-scoped isolation and runtime-injected hooks. In the same repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can race and corrupt work, with no locking mechanism documented in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent commits or edits can conflict.
IF either agent writes generated files while the other edits the same paths, last-writer-wins corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate branches to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use a clean worktree per agent.
Review git status before merging outputs.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestrator-level coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can produce code changes and shell actions, while oh-my-openagent has team messaging/task tools and can act on project code and session history. If one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or messages. The profiles do not prove blind trust, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF oh-my-openagent consumes Claude Code output without verification, downstream actions may amplify mistakes.
IF Claude Code uses oh-my-openagent-generated code or instructions as authoritative, bad edits can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require tests before accepting generated code.
Use explicit source labels on inter-agent messages.
Limit one agent to suggestion-only mode.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before task/message APIs.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and local files; oh-my-openagent handles provider auth prompts, telemetry, and session history. The profiles show different data-handling surfaces and retention-adjacent telemetry, but no direct residency or certification mismatch is documented. That makes a compliance gap plausible, though not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace, both agents may process it under different logging or retention regimes.
IF telemetry or session history includes sensitive content, it may be retained outside the operator’s intended policy.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared repo.
Review telemetry settings before use.
Separate auth prompts from project files.
Document retention expectations for both tools.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both agents.
